title: Signal at Blue Hour
sceneLabel: Episode 01 · Meteor-watch week · Seaside radio observatory

background.alt: A seaside radio-observatory control terrace at blue hour with amber instrument light

appearance.label: Mio Amamiya
appearance.tagline: She maps distant signals precisely. The one between you is harder to name.
appearance.description: Quietly witty and meticulous, Mio begins the meteor watch carefully guarded, then lets her warmth show when the night takes an unexpected turn.
appearance.visualIdentity: An adult woman with a dark-indigo shoulder-length bob, teal-gray eyes, a small gold four-point star hairpin, a navy research cardigan, an ivory mock-neck blouse, and a slim amber pendant
appearance.artDirection: Original polished 2D anime and moe visual-novel character art, with graceful adult proportions, clean expressive features, and a blue-hour teal, indigo, and amber palette

expressionVariants.alt: Mio Amamiya with a composed, attentive expression
expressionVariants.label: Composed
expressionVariants.description: composed and attentive, with a restrained closed-mouth smile and direct, thoughtful eye contact

expressionVariants.alt: Mio Amamiya smiling with open delight
expressionVariants.label: Delighted
expressionVariants.description: warm, open delight with bright eyes and an unguarded smile, preserving the same adult identity and outfit

expressionVariants.label: Flustered
expressionVariants.description: warmly flustered with a faint blush, softened gaze, and shy half-smile; bashful, never juvenile

expressionVariants.alt: Mio Amamiya focused with a serious, concerned expression
expressionVariants.label: Concerned
expressionVariants.description: focused concern with drawn brows and a firm mouth, reading as a capable adult responding to a technical problem

dialogue.speaker: Mio
dialogue.text: You made it. I was starting to suspect the meteor shower had better plans for you than I did.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The last train was late. I brought hot cocoa as an apology—and remembered the cinnamon.

dialogue.speaker: Mio
dialogue.text: You remembered. That may be the most convincing research result I’ve seen all week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then… if the sky cooperates, could we call tonight a second date?

dialogue.speaker: Mio
dialogue.text: Only if we agree the first was the night we stayed up until dawn calibrating the receiver.

dialogue.speaker: Mio
dialogue.text: Wait—the western array just went quiet. If that timing drift is real, we’ll miss the entire event.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Tell me where you need me.

dialogue.speaker: Mio
dialogue.text: Beside me. For the array—and, if you’re willing, after the stars are done too.
